#2982. Black Friday Porch Pirates Don’t Care About Your Doorbell Camera. Follow This Expert Plan Now

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Soda was stolen moments after delivery. One expert says it's a common tactic.

Doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up. Some porch pirates don’t care about being caught on camera as long as they’re able to steal your package, and it’s unlikely that law enforcement will track down the stolen goods.

That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera. It wasn’t expensive tech or a snazzy holiday gift — it was $36 worth of soda.

“When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper said. “When I pulled up the Ring footage, I saw the delivery happen on video, but then, 10 minutes later, a man in a blue hooded coat who’s intentionally hiding his face shows up and grabs the box.”

Package theft cases like this happen year-round, with CNET findings showing that 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or have stopped an attempted theft. And experts predict more stolen packages during the holidays, when thieves expect more deliveries.

So, don’t give thieves a chance. Now’s the time to make a plan to keep your Black Friday and Cyber Monday packages out of sight. But what tactics actually work if doorbell cameras don’t? Here’s what you should know about porch piracy and how to lessen your chances of package theft.

Cooper’s Amazon order was scheduled to arrive between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m. — when it’s dark, but she knew she would be home. But thieves were already out lurking during those hours. Cooper said the thief followed the driver and stole the package. She saw the thief stealing the package on her Ring security camera system.

Greg Zakowicz, Omnisend’s e-commerce and retail advisor, said Cooper’s package-theft incident is fairly typical, unfortunately — especially during the holiday season.

“Thieves know as well as shoppers that orders increase during this time, and often, the packages are more likely to contain more valuable items,” said Zakowicz. “Shoppers during this time look to take advantage of deep discounts for not only gifts but themselves, making the package a potential goldmine for thieves.”

There are a few steps you can take to lessen the likelihood of porch piracy. Zakowicz recommends using options like in-store pickups, post office boxes, in-garage delivery or deliveries to your workplace.

That advice is especially important for expensive tech you plan to have delivered to your home unless someone will be there to grab the package immediately.

“While it may be less convenient, it’s a small price to pay to not have the hassle of gifts and expensive items going missing at the busiest shopping time of the year,” said Zackowicz.

Also ask your retailers not to ship the item in the manufacturer’s packaging. Some retailers, like Amazon and Target, will clearly display this before shipping because it could be an easy hint for thieves to guess what it is — especially if it’s tech. Even though this won’t stop porch pirates from being curious about what’s in the box, it may make them think about the effort and risk versus the potential reward, Zakowicz said.

If you want another option to have packages delivered to your home, consider scheduling your deliveries for a time you know you’ll be available. For instance, you can set up an Amazon Day to have all of your Amazon packages delivered at once so you can plan accordingly.

CNET found that US adults have mixed feelings about how effectively security cameras deter porch pirates: 11% of US adults believe they don’t deter them, while 9% use security cameras to get proof — not prevent it.

Regardless of your home security measures, don’t assume you’re safe from porch pirates just because you have a doorbell camera, and don’t use it as a means of keeping an eye on your package if you’re busy or not home. Instead, when you see motion detection, that’s a sign to grab it right away.

“The most common misunderstanding is that having security cameras will prevent thieves from stealing packages,” said Zakowicz. “Thieves are thieves because being caught is not their biggest worry. They also know porch piracy is not at the top of most officers’ day-to-day public service worries. Often, by the time the report is made, thieves are long gone.”

Unfortunately, thieves may find other ways to steal packages, since their tactics are constantly changing. If that happens to you, there are a few steps you should take right away.

File a police report of the incident first. Be prepared to share information, including a description of the thief, and the make and model of the vehicle, with the police and your community so they can be vigilant of the thief.

But don’t get your hopes up that the thief will be caught. Zakowicz said it’s rare that porch theft cases get solved.

“Police aren’t necessarily dedicating resources to solving porch pirates who stole a new stuffed animal or board game. However, it’s important for them to understand areas seeing an uptick in thefts, as they can be more alert to suspicious activity,” said Zakowicz. And the retailer may request it.

After filing, Zakowicz says to report the theft to the carrier and retailer. Carriers may use the data to assess future likelihood of package theft incidents and it could help instruct delivery drivers to carefully hide packages. Retailers may also be able to assist with a replacement.

Cooper filed a police report with her local police department, which allowed her to upload the Ring video of the theft and acknowledged receipt. She’s not expecting the thief to be caught, but figures that her report could possibly help in some way.

“I live in a pretty safe neighborhood in Amazon’s own hometown, but their delivery trucks are on our street dropping off packages every day,” she said. “It’s got to be a banquet for hungry thieves.”

She reached out to her neighbors to tell them about the theft, and one reported that she, too, had had a package stolen a week earlier.

Cooper says she did not intentionally choose the early-morning drop-off time, but it was the only time Amazon offered for her delivery. Since then, she’s seen Amazon try to offer that same time and has chosen not to order an item rather than be forced to use that dark, quiet delivery slot.

Immediately after the theft, Amazon was less than helpful, routing her to an AI agent who said it understood the situation was upsetting but that it wouldn’t be able to do anything for four days. When she checked back, Amazon agreed to refund her for the item, but kept insisting on labeling the package as “missing” and asked her to report back if she “found” it.

“I hope the driver doesn’t get in trouble for a supposedly ‘missing’ package,” she said. “It unnerves me that she was being followed by a thief. Who knows how long he followed that truck and how many packages he scooped up?”

#2981. Novo Nordisk vs. Vertex Pharmaceuticals: Which Pharma Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Novo Nordisk's obesity drugs and Vertex's cystic fibrosis franchise pull in very different directions, and the valuation gap between them is wide enough to change the answer.

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 28, 2026 at 11:12AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Novo Nordisk ›

The healthcare landscape is evolving rapidly as chronic diseases and genetic disorders demand innovative treatments, putting Novo Nordisk A/S (NVO +0.24%) and Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX -5.24%) at the forefront of the sector.

Novo Nordisk specializes in metabolic care with a massive global manufacturing footprint, while Vertex Pharmaceuticals focuses on high-value therapies for rare conditions. This comparison examines their different business models and financial health to help you decide which company better suits your investment goals.

Novo Nordisk is a global healthcare company that focuses primarily on chronic conditions, including diabetes, obesity, and rare diseases. The company reached more than 46.5 million people living with serious illnesses, according to its latest annual report, and is supported by a workforce of about 69,505 employees. Its strategy centers on leveraging its deep expertise in protein engineering to produce GLP-1 medications that have become central to modern weight management and diabetes care.

The company's financial performance remains robust as demand for its core products continues to climb globally. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $48.8 billion, representing growth of approximately 5.7% compared to the prior twelve-month period. During this same time frame, the company generated net income of $16.6 billion, resulting in a healthy net margin of about 33.9%, which measures how much of every dollar in sales remains as profit after all expenses.

On the balance sheet, the company maintains a stable financial position that supports its ongoing research in biotech vs pharma innovations. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.7x, meaning the company uses about 70 cents of debt for every dollar of shareholder equity. Its current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, was around 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was $4.2 billion, representing the cash remaining after the company pays for its operations and capital investments.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals is a biotechnology leader that has redefined the treatment of cystic fibrosis with a portfolio of highly effective medicines. Beyond its core market, the company is commercializing new therapies for sickle cell disease and acute pain, diversifying its revenue streams. Vertex sells its medicines primarily to specialty pharmacies and major wholesalers, maintaining important collaboration agreements with CRISPR Therapeutics (CRSP -0.45%), Moderna (MRNA +3.53%), and Zai Lab (ZLAB +2.77%).

The company has demonstrated strong top-line momentum as it expands into new therapeutic areas. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $13.0 billion, an increase of about 10.5% over the previous period. Vertex reported GAAP net income of $4.0 billion for those twelve months, achieving a net margin of approximately 30.7%. This indicates a consistent ability to convert a high percentage of sales into actual profit for shareholders.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals also has a very conservative balance sheet and high liquidity. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.1x, and the current ratio was approximately 2.9x. A current ratio above 1.0 typically suggests a company is well-positioned to meet its immediate financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was $3.2 billion, providing ample capital for its collaborations with partners like Entrada Therapeutics (TRDA +0.87%).

Novo Nordisk A/S faces intense competition in the metabolic health space, particularly as other pharmaceutical giants launch rival obesity treatments. The company must also manage potential manufacturing constraints as it scales production to meet massive global demand for its injectable medications. Furthermore, government initiatives to reduce drug prices in major markets could impact the pricing power the company currently enjoys for its blockbuster therapies.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals carries significant revenue concentration risk because it depends on its cystic fibrosis treatments for the majority of its sales. The company is also subject to regulatory and pricing pressures, including potential payment limits set by prescription drug affordability boards. Additionally, its research and development activities involve significant uncertainty, particularly regarding the success of clinical trials and the manufacturing complexity of its newer cell and gene therapies.

Novo Nordisk A/S currently trades at lower multiples than Vertex Pharmaceuticals for both earnings and sales, suggesting the market may be applying a higher growth premium to Vertex.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals continues to benefit from its focus on cystic fibrosis (CF). It recently launched Alyftrek, a once-daily, next-in-class, triple-combination CF regimen. The treatment is seen encouragingly by investors. Alyftrek marks a notable improvement to the twice-daily dosage of Vertex's other CF products and was approved in Australia, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, the U.K., and Canada over the course of 2025, after the U.S. approved it in 2024. Plenty more jurisdictions are evaluating the treatment today. In the U.S., label extensions (the expansion of FDA approval for use) mean Vertex can treat 95% of people with cystic fibrosis in the country today.

Vertex has expanded into treating other conditions. Povetacicept, an investigational recombinant fusion protein therapeutic, continues to show best-in-class potential as a treatment for three chronic autoimmune diseases: IgA nephropathy (IgAN), primary membranous nephropathy (pMN), and generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG). The FDA has granted its Breakthrough Therapy Designation for IgAN, with potential approval by Nov. 30 this year, as well as Fast Track Designation for pMN. If approved across the IgAN, pMN, and gMG indications, peak annual sales could reach $4 billion to $7 billion, according to equity analyst firm Argus.

For fiscal 2026, Vertex sales should rise about 10% to $13.3 billion, with net income coming in a little lower, at $3.6 billion. In 2027, analysts expect sales of $14.7 billion and net income of $4.5 billion.

Novo Nordisk has the blockbuster drugs Wegovy and Ozempic (the same drug marketed for different purposes), but faces investor doubts about its market position given a deal with the federal government to lower prices for the GLP-1s, the emergence of generic competitors, and the apparent advances by Eli Lilly & Co. (LLY +0.01%) in developing weight loss drugs expected to be superior to Novo's offerings.

Still, the introduction of the once-a-day Wegovy pill in the U.S. has been a resounding success, and the business has a patent on the injectable Ozempic/Wegovy until 2032, providing it with a competitive moat. Still, Wall Street sees sales declining by about 3% in fiscal 2026, with net income contracting by 4% as pricing pressures slightly erode margins. Long-term, analysts expect the company to reverse the 2026 decline and resume growth as new products come online.

The glory days of the GLP-1 boom could be in Novo Nordisk's rearview mirror, something Wall Street thinks is a possibility given the stock's low forward P/E. Vertex offers growth at a reasonable premium and is the wiser buy, given Novo's sales stumble.

#2980. Gen Z is the least interested in AI at work – and it’s not even close

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Younger workers don't find AI useful, according to a recent survey.

Generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

Gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them

“Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” said Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

Around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it

It’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

“We need to show young workers how AI can strengthen their work, provide clear guidelines and training, and give them opportunities to practice using it and build the skills they’ll need as leaders,” Forster said.

#2978. 4 Security Devices I Rely On for Front Porch and Delivery Protection

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Home security starts with your front door and porch. This is the tech that I think everyone should have.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason. That’s where burglars first try, too, and research shows thieves can be deterred with the presence of a security cam — but security technology can do so much more.

From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without. Take a look to see what your porch could use, too, and the tech options I recommend looking at.

Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock. Smart locks allow you to control your front door lock from anywhere using your phone, as well as creating temporary passes for guests. They can support digital wallet keys for touchless unlocking, and many have keypads or fingerprint readers. Plus, you can enable settings like auto-locking, so you never have to worry about forgetting to lock the door.

Smart locks come in two flavors: retrofits that leave your deadbolt largely intact and only replace your indoor thumb turn, and full deadbolt replacements that give you new locking power, inside and out. Don’t worry about installation: If you’ve never installed a deadbolt before, the process is generally easy and doesn’t take much time. I have a full guide where you can find more details.

Say goodbye to dusty doorbells of the past. Today’s high-tech doorbells do far more than chime: Video doorbells keep an eye on your front porch, while also giving you a two-way audio intercom right on your phone to hold a conversation — or even let an LLM do the talking for you.

Video doorbells also have particularly useful object recognition features, sometimes even for free. That includes recognizing packages and alerting you whenever one shows up at your door, or when one suddenly vanishes. Video storage options can save recordings of key events, so you can check who came to the door if you need to.

These advanced doorbells come in both wired and wireless versions. I’m a fan of the battery-powered, wireless models, which you can set and angle to get just the right look at your porch, doormat and other key places. Many can also work with your current door chime, although you probably don’t need it anymore with phone-based chimes.

Yale’s delivery boxes are larger, so you need room for them in the right spots.

Package theft concerns have reignited a centuries-old tradition of protecting mail. Today’s modern delivery boxes are specifically designed to allow delivery people to put packages inside, but make it difficult or impossible for thieves to take packages out, through clever lock models, auto-locking, smart controls and other various tricks.

I’ve been using a delivery box myself for a couple of years and find it very handy, as long as you have the space by your door. Some versions even come weighted or screwed down if you’re worried about a porch pirate absconding with the entire box. It’s a good idea to put notes in your deliveries to use the box, since despite signs not all delivery people will notice it’s there.

As a final plus, these boxes also keep your packages protected from the elements, which is nice when you live in an area that gets frequent winter snowstorms, as I do.

Smart bulbs are cheap, support multiple voice assistants and have lots of fun tricks.

Where front doors exist, there’s usually a light nearby, like an overhead porch light or a wall-mounted lamp, to illuminate the entryway and surrounding area. These lights can also get a major makeover if you switch to an LED smart bulb, which are available as both BR30 floodlights and standard A19 home bulbs.

These lights also give you phone app controls, which is more important than it might seem. With my apps, I can control brightness, set schedules for bulbs to turn on or off, and even adjust the color to whatever I want, say for a holiday event. All it takes is screwing in the bulb and connecting it to Wi-Fi, so you can be done in seconds.

If you feel like experimenting, you can usually link smart bulbs to other devices, too. For example, you could set the light to turn on automatically when a smart lock is unlocked, or when a security system is disarmed.

Now that your front porch is up to date, take a look at the latest home AI tricks I’ve found are actually worth using and how to get them.

#2977. A Recession Could Be Coming in 2027. Here's Why I'm Not Worried.

A common-sense plan can help you prepare for the next recession.

By Dana George – Nov 28, 2026 at 11:15AM EST

While recessions are part of the normal economic cycle, that view minimizes their effect on everyday Americans. Not counting the Great Depression of 1929 through 1933, there have been 15 recessions over the last 100 years. The U.S. has managed to survive them all, but that doesn't mean it's been easy.

Here are some of the signs economists use to forecast a recession:

Given the number of factors at play in the U.S. today, it's no surprise that some are convinced we're entering a recession. Whether that's true or not, here's why I'm not worried.

No matter how or why it happens, I plan for the next recession in the same, uncomplicated way. There's nothing magical about my plan, other than that it touches all the bases.

I know two things about recessions. First, they don't last forever. The longest recession in the past 100 years was the Great Recession of 2007 to 2009, an economic mess that lasted 18 months. The shortest lasted two months, during the COVID-19 pandemic.

I also know that panic leads to making irrational investment decisions, and irrational decisions can turn a temporary drop into a permanent loss. Selling investments after they've fallen locks in a lower price and likely means I'll miss the recovery. In fact, I keep investing to take advantage of bargain prices caused by those who abandon the market during a recession.

To be clear, a recession in 2027 is possible, but it's not inevitable. A forecast can only act as a warning light, not a verdict. I'm not dismissing the risks, but I am looking at what the forecasts say. Although ominous signs are clearly visible, major forecasts in November 2026 still expect the U.S. economy to keep growing, despite recent AI drama.

Whether you're planning for a recession, a bear market, or other unexpected occurrence, remain diversified, stay calm, and remember it won't last forever.

Anthropic's new 'install as app' feature makes it easy to turn your Claude artifacts into desktop apps on your computer - with some limitations.

Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude plans and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks users do regularly, especially at work. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

Also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok

The update clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

“If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic said.

Claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

First, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid plans, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free

Full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic said, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and update the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise plans, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

“Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the company said.

For Claude Enterprise plans, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is the first dividend pick. Earlier this month, the company paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share. At an annualized dividend of $7.12 per share, CVX offers a dividend yield of about 3.5%.

Mehta also noted Chevron's efforts to deploy new technologies, especially in shale and tight-oil operations. CVX is focused on boosting productivity and efficiency to maximize free cash flow, he added.

Initiatives such as artificial lift optimization, AI and machine learning, and advanced chemical treatments are expected to improve recovery by about 10% in new wells. Enterprise Products Partners (EPD) is a master limited partnership (MLP) that provides midstream energy services to producers and consumers of natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals. With a quarterly cash distribution of 56 cents per common unit ($2.24 per common unit annualized), EPD offers a yield of about 6%.

Following a recent call with the company, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on EPD with a price target of $42. The analyst slightly lowered her estimates for the second half of 2026, citing margin and volume normalization, though demand dynamics remain strong.

While the 5-star analyst expects a sequential decline due to normal seasonality and normalization following high spreads in the first half of the year, she still expects EPD to report another solid quarter (Q3 2026) and enter 2027 with a favorable setup. Ahead of Q3 earnings, Scotto expects investors to focus on export demand durability, EPD's ability to profit from spot cargo sales and growth in Permian volumes.

Scotto continues to expect $150 million of common unit buybacks per quarter in the second half of 2026. She expects buybacks to increase to $200 million per quarter in 2027, as capex spending declines and free cash flow improves.

In total, Scotto is bullish on EPD and views it as a core MLP holding that has both offensive and defensive characteristics. The analyst praised EPD's diverse asset base as ensuring stable cash flows. "Furthermore, the partnership's multi-year organic growth backlog helps provide visibility on long-term distribution growth," Scotto said.

Scotto ranks No. 199 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 15.9%. See Enterprise Products Partners Financials on TipRanks.

#2970. Does the S&P 500 Really Deserve Its December Reputation?

The market's current losing streak has investors really wishing for some holiday cheer to close out the year.

By Neil Patel – Nov 28, 2026 at 11:27AM EST

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›

The S&P 500 index (^GSPC +1.60%) needs a pick-me-up. As of Nov. 27, the benchmark is trading 7% below its peak. A lot of attention is going to the tech sector and artificial intelligence stocks. Investors are becoming more concerned not only about the spending boom's durability but also about what the ultimate returns will be. The market hates uncertainty.

But December, and its holiday cheer, is around the corner. It's a month that could bring some optimism. Since 1926, the total U.S. stock market (measured by the CRSP Value-Weighted Market Index) has produced an average total return of 1.6% in December, making it the third-best month historically, not far behind November and July. As 2026 comes to a close, the investment community is desperately hoping the odds of this trend holding up are in their favor.

Does the S&P 500 index really deserve its winning December reputation? Let's zoom in to a more recent time frame. Here's what the past 10 years suggest.

From the last close in November to the last close in December, the S&P 500 rose in six of the past 10 years (2016 through 2025). That's a winning record. But it's much closer to a coin flip than the month's festive reputation suggests.

The size of the moves tells the real story, and it isn't a cheerful one. The index's average December price return over that stretch was just 0.05%.

One month did most of the damage. In December 2018, the S&P 500 plunged 9.2%, its worst December since 1931. Strip out that year, and the average for the other nine Decembers climbs to about 1.1%.

Recent years haven't been much kinder, either. The benchmark fell in three of the last four Decembers. It dropped 5.9% in 2022 and 2.5% in 2024. Last year, it was essentially flat, ending the month down 0.05%.

The 2018 setup deserves a closer look. The Federal Reserve was still raising interest rates then, delivering its fourth hike of the year on Dec. 19 and signaling two more were likely in 2019. Investors worried that tighter policy would choke off growth.

That rhymes with the current backdrop. The central bank raised rates in September for the first time since July 2023, and its projections indicated another hike before year-end.

Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury yield is just under 5%. It has finished above 5% on 27 days this year, the most since 2007. Higher yields offer investors a credible alternative to stocks and, theoretically, put pressure on valuations.

But 2018 also shows what happened to investors who stayed the course. The S&P 500 soared 29% in 2019. To be fair, it had help on the macro front. The Fed paused its hikes and then cut rates three times that year.

Still, nobody knew that on Christmas Eve 2018. The decade's worst December turned out to be a fantastic buying opportunity.

The S&P 500 index heads toward December near correction territory, dipping as much as 11.6% below its Oct. 6 record in late November. After that kind of losing streak, it's understandable to hope for a holiday bounce. Building a strategy around one, however, is not the right move.

One month's seasonality is a weak signal. The past 10 Decembers included three notable declines. Yet the index is still up 224% since the end of 2016 before dividends (and 277% with dividends reinvested). Trying to avoid a bad December requires two correct predictions. You have to know when to get out. And you need to know when to get back in. Investors who tried to dodge the bad months would surely have missed some of the good ones, too.

There's an obvious lesson. Long-term investors in a low-cost fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF are better served by sticking to a regular investing schedule than by betting on a year-end rally. Time in the market still beats timing the calendar.

When our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 792%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 202% for the S&P 500.

They just revealed what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy right now, available when you join Stock Advisor.

#2969. Apple Brings Its iPhone Broadcasting to Formula 1 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Apple, the F1 broadcast provider in the US, is supplementing coverage with its own iPhone cameras.

When you watch a Formula 1 race on TV, the screen is packed with lap times, driver stats and real-time video from inside the cars and around the track. During the Las Vegas Grand Prix race, some of those views were captured with iPhone Pro phones and transmitted in real time over T-Mobile’s 5G network.

Using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty. Apple has been shooting its event videos and ad spots with iPhone Pro models outfitted with cinema-grade lenses, SSD storage and broadcasting gear for several years now. In May, Apple broadcast a Major League Soccer game shot with iPhones strapped to professional lenses, following it up with a Major League Baseball game in September using its own camera hardware,

But compared to a ballpark, F1 ratchets up the complexity, especially in Las Vegas. At the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the race track snakes 3.9 miles through the city’s downtown core. Its route includes the famed Strip (South Las Vegas Boulevard), where most of the big hotels are.

“We control everything on baseball, so we can do whatever we want there,” said Royce Dickerson, executive producer of live sports at Apple TV. “We did 14 iPhones on top of our normal camera complement” during the baseball broadcast. He noted that 10 of those were connected via T-Mobile’s 5G wireless network.

But integrating iPhone cameras into an F1 broadcast, even for the sport’s US broadcaster, is more of a challenge. “I’ve been doing TV production for 20-plus years,” said Dickerson, “and the scale of their operation is unlike anything I’ve seen before.”

Because F1 has agreements with other camera partners, Dickerson did not specify how many iPhones were set up around the track. Neither Apple nor T-Mobile explained where the iPhones were placed in order to capture the speedy F1 vehicles racing around the Vegas Strip. I suspect they were likely deployed in more conventional environments for smartphone cameras, like the team garages and roving to catch celebrities in the paddock area and in the stands, though the iPhone setups wirelessly broadcasting footage at earlier sporting events means they could be easily placed in many locations on and above the streets.

“You really have to work hard to earn the fans’ attention [and] that viewing experience,” said Dickerson. “How are you getting your fans closer to their favorite athlete, to their favorite driver, to their team, to the personalities that surround the sport?”

In the T-Mobile zone at the Sphere – an area sponsored by the carrier and open to T-Mobile customers – at least 10 iPhone cameras were used to cover a stage where concerts played between events. That number is based on a diagram shared during a tour of T-Mobile’s Tech Trailer, where the company’s event coordinators stay on top of things like crowd movements and line lengths.

Dean Locke, executive director of broadcast, media and race operations at Formula 1, sees the combination of multiple cameras streaming wirelessly over 5G as an essential component to the Las Vegas race.

“If we just did cameras at a low level, the fences and track, we haven’t done a very good job,” said Locke. “How can we open up stages, concerts and all of the activities? Each race has a real kind of personality to it. You can only [capture that personality] with huge amounts of cameras, huge amounts of technology.”

If Apple is using iPhones to record live sports, are they recording any of that footage using spatial video for viewing in the Vision Pro? Imagine getting a track-level view of a group of Formula 1 cars speeding past at 200 miles per hour with Apple’s depth effect. “[There’s] nothing at this time I can say about it,” said Dickerson.

Editors’ note: Jeff Carlson’s travel costs for the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix were covered by T-Mobile. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

#2968. Alphabet Stock Is Near a 52-Week Low. Here's Why I'd Buy the Dip.

Wall Street is fixated on Alphabet's capex spending, but it may be overlooking what that money is building.

By John Ballard – Nov 28, 2026 at 11:35AM EST

Shares of Alphabet (GOOGL +0.68%) (GOOG +0.54%), the parent of Google Search, YouTube, and Gemini, sank to a 52-week low of $260.69 this week, and while they bounced somewhat on Friday’s shortened trading day to close at $272.44,  that was still about 15.4% below their close on Oct. 28, the day it reported third-quarter results. Shares are also well off their high of $404.47.

Investors’ worry appears to be related to the company’s massive capital expenditures. Alphabet is on track to invest $195 billion to $205 billion into building data centers and other infrastructure this year, and expects to spend even more in 2027. In Q3, that spending pushed the company’s free cash flow to negative $9 billion.

But that spending is building one of Alphabet's most promising new businesses. Here's why I'd buy the dip.

Alphabet designs its own custom AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), and now sells complete TPU systems, including networking and software, to external customers. TPU system sales were a meaningful contributor to Google Cloud's growth last quarter, though management said Cloud's growth was also incredibly strong without them.

The bigger payoff is still ahead. CFO Anat Ashkenazi expects TPU system sales to keep scaling in the fourth quarter, "followed by a meaningful revenue ramp in 2027." That could give Google Cloud significant runway for growth over the next several years.

Demand looks broad. CEO Sundar Pichai said Alphabet is seeing strong demand for TPU systems across a wide range of customers. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said the new TPU 8t and 8i offer up to 2.7 times better training performance and 80% better price performance for inference, the work of running AI models, than the previous generation. That gives customers more reason to buy.

Importantly, Google Cloud’s profits are soaring. Its operating income more than tripled from a year ago to $11 billion in the third quarter, and its operating margin rose to 36% from 24%. So the investments Google is making in bringing more data center capacity online and in TPUs are paying off.

Analysts expect Alphabet's earnings to grow by about 14% annually over the next several years. At Friday's price, that's about 18 times 2027 earnings estimates -- a reasonable price for this kind of growth and in line with the S&P 500 (^GSPC +1.60%) forward P/E.

The risk is that the market will continue to punish the stock for that heavy AI spending, which continues to weigh on free cash flow. But Alphabet only buys parts to build TPU inventory after customers sign contracts for the hardware, which means it converts these investments into revenue quickly.

Alphabet is one of the most dominant tech companies trading at a fair valuation. Given the momentum in its cloud and TPU business, buying the dip should reward investors in 2027 and beyond.

#2967. This Portable Spot Cleaner From Bissell Is an Affordable Alternative to the Shark StainForce on Black Friday

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

You don't need to buy a full-sized carpet cleaner for your pet's messes.

A carpet cleaner may not be your first thought for a Black Friday purchase, but it’s actually a great time to buy one, since one of my favorite new cleaners I’ve tested is on sale. The Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner is $85 at Amazon, down from its usual $130 price. That’s a $45 savings and, according to Amazon, its lowest price in 365 days. That’s considerably cheaper than the Shark StainForce, which goes for around $200 and is $130 for Black Friday.

The Bissell Little Green cleaner offers tons of cleaning power in a small package at a reasonable price, though there are one or two catches regarding portability and setup that are worth knowing about before you decide which one to buy.

The Bissell Little Green Mini is a powerful portable spot cleaner. / CNET/Ajay Kumar

The Bissell Little Green Mini is a corded portable spot cleaner, but it’s still lightweight at 7 pounds. Setup is definitely a little more involved, with a clean water tank that you need to mix cleaning solution into and the need to have an AC outlet somewhere in the area. The trade-off is a significantly deeper, more powerful cleaning than what you get with a handheld battery-powered spot cleaner like the Shark StainForce. Using the Little Green on the toughest and oldest dried stains left by my pukey old man cat left me impressed with just how deeply it cleaned my carpets. The pristine result makes this corded cleaner well worth the extra setup, and even at full price ($130), you won’t find fault with its power or portability.

At $85, its lowest price in a year on Amazon, the Bissell Little Green Mini is an easy buy if you have pets and carpet.

Shark StainForce cleaning a stain off my carpet. / Ajay Kumar/CNET

The Shark StainForce is a unique handheld vacuum because it doesn’t just clean dry messes — it’s primarily intended to remove stains and wet messes. It resembles other handheld vacuums, but comes with a caddy and a custom Shark stain cleaner that mixes a deep cleaner and oxy cleaner in the spray bottle to lift stains.

It works incredibly well — I was blown away by how easily it lifted the worst messes off my white carpets. It removed yellow cat puke stains, wine stains and tomato sauce off both the carpet and couch. It works equally well for older dried stains and wet stains, using a mix of the stain cleaner spray and agitation with the included rubber scrubbing brush head that suctions up the mess at the same time. There’s also a smaller nozzle-brush cleaner included for tight spots.

The StainForce will suction up dry waste like cat hair and chunks of half-digested cat food, but the waste tank is fairly small, and it’s not really meant for dry cleaning of a large area due to the limited battery life.

The tank will also need to be cleaned out and dried after every use because wet messes will fester and smell if left too long. With all that said, this is the only portable spot cleaner I’ve seen with the design and usability of a handheld vacuum, which makes it an excellent choice if your primary need is portable spot cleaning. The $200 price may sound steep, but I’ve never seen a compact cleaner as good at tackling such tough stains.

I love the Shark StainForce for its service as a grab-and-go cleaner. It’s cordless, it lives in its caddy ready to go, and for a fresh spill I can spray, scrub, and suction in under a minute with no setup at all. I’ve used it on my cats’ worst messes, including hairballs, vomit from eating too fast, and dirty paws tracked in from the litter box. It works remarkably well for something so small and it’s still the go-to cleaner for my wife and I. The dual-spray bottle that comes with it does an incredible job of lifting stains, even from my white carpet.

Here I am scrubbing away with the StainForce powered on. You can still see some stain, but it’s going away.

The Little Green Mini is a different kind of machine, and that difference shows in the results. On a day when my cats were in rare form and decided to throw up on the bedroom carpet three times in a row, I knew a small portable cleaner like the StainForce wouldn’t cut it, not with the sheer quantity of debris they’d left behind.

I pulled the Bissell Little Green, which, worth acknowledging, is corded. That means more setup: fill the 16-ounce clean tank with water and the included Oxy formula, plug in the 12-foot cord, and work within reach of the cord and its 4-foot hose. It’s still light at just 7 pounds, and it has a useful handle for moving it from room to room.

The StainForce, by contrast, has no clean tank at all. You spray from a separate bottle and only a tiny dirty-water collection tank of under 5 ounces, with about 15 minutes of battery before it needs a recharge. The Mini’s clean and dirty tanks (16 and 13.5 ounces) are much bigger, and because it’s plugged in, it never runs out of power mid-clean.

That proved to be the lifesaver in cleaning my cat’s horrible messes. The Bissell generously saturated the stain with its built-in sprayer that can dispense water and cleaning solution straight from the hose. The hose digs in deep, rinsing and pulling stains, mess and dirt from deep out of the carpet layers. The larger chunks were safely suctioned into the dirty tank, along with the used water.

What I can say is that it did an excellent job of deep-cleaning stains from the carpet — noticeably deeper than the StainForce. It completely removed our cat’s mess, with no trace left behind, though our carpets were left a little moist. My wife’s verdict was that she’s never seen the carpets so clean before and she audibly wondered if it was worth investing in a full-size carpet cleaner because clearly the StainForce and vacuuming aren’t cutting it.

If you want the fastest possible cleanup for a fresh spill, get the Shark StainForce; it’s hard to beat a cordless cleaner with zero setup. For a smaller mess that I just want to get off my carpet, the StainForce more than does its job. But if your problem is stains that have soaked into the carpet, the Bissell Little Green Mini is the better cleaner, and at $85 on Black Friday — its lowest Amazon price in a year — it’s $45 less than the StainForce right now. It’s the one I’d buy for a house with pets, kids and carpets where you don’t want a big and bulky carpet cleaner and don’t want to worry about running out of charge for a bigger mess.

#2966. Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

Chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

"CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the company if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

"Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

#2965. What Nvidia Investors Should Watch During Jensen Huang's Senate Hearing

Jensen Huang's testimony is about export controls, not just one executive. Here is what an owner of the stock can listen for.

By Patrick Sanders – Nov 28, 2026 at 11:35AM EST

Nvidia's (NVDA +0.80%) board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov. 23, less than two weeks after he resigned. Next comes Washington: closed-door sessions with three House committees on Dec. 1, then a public Senate Banking Committee hearing on Dec. 3. For shareholders, the question is narrower than the headlines. How much rides on one executive, and how well does Nvidia control where its chips go?

Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

In its Nov. 23 release, Nvidia said the board was satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings. It also said it received input from senior levels of the U.S. government and is confident his return poses no national security risk.

The company said an independent committee will finish its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The board has also formed a national security and export control committee, and Nvidia is searching for a chief compliance officer.

The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export controls, the rules on which advanced chips can be sold abroad. Its questions go to where Nvidia is allowed to sell.

Another outside view arrived Nov. 25. S&P Global Ratings said it is considering cutting Nvidia's credit rating one notch, to the fourth-highest level on its scale, citing "key man risk," meaning heavy reliance on Huang, and weak succession planning. TechCrunch noted that Nvidia backs the debt of companies building data centers for artificial intelligence. A lower rating could raise their borrowing costs.

The risk to a calm reading is that the board's confidence is not the last word. TechCrunch reported that the hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify.

When he does, listen for specifics rather than reassurance. Notice who is accountable for tracking where Nvidia's chips end up. Then watch for the compliance hire and for S&P's decision, which it expects within 90 days.

#2964. Apple Stays Winning as Smartphone Sales Continue to Slump

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Memory prices continue to be a problem, especially for cheaper phone sales.

RAM prices are continuing to put the squeeze on smartphone sales, and even people who typically buy less expensive phones appear to be holding off on upgrading.

According to a new report from Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 9% compared to the same period in 2025. The report attributed the drop to rising memory costs, which are hurting sales at the low end of the Android phone market.

In terms of market share, Samsung held steady at around 25%, while Motorola, Google and other companies saw their slice of the pie decline. Where did those sales go, you might be wondering? Unsurprisingly, Apple’s broad range of iPhone models — from the 17E to its newest foldable flagship, the $1,999 iPhone Duo — bumped the company’s share of the smartphone market from 50% to 57% since last year.

Smartphone-makers with cheaper phone lineups suffered due to component costs, particularly memory, eating into their margins. “There, OEMs have little room to absorb a higher bill of materials without raising prices or cutting volume,” said Counterpoint Senior Analyst Emily Herbert.

The slowdown in phone sales has been happening all year. In the last quarter, the market slumped by 20%, more than was expected at the time. The build-out of data centers to support the ever-expanding AI industry has led to shortages of memory components. In turn, the prices of those components have spiked, raising prices of not just smartphones, but game consoles, PCs and other electronics.

Read more: Best Black Friday iPhone Deals

Black Friday, Cyber Monday and the Christmas gift-giving season typically mean strong phone sales for companies like Apple and Samsung. But the memory component crisis isn’t going to go away that quickly, and prices of phones are still higher overall.

Counterpoint predicts that smartphone sales will remain weak in the next quarter and that US carriers may be more selective about the promotions they offer this year. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are also seeing declining sales and customers are getting choosier about committing to phones that often cost more than $1,000. People are also looking to second-hand and refurbished phones instead of buying new.

“Consumers are timing their purchases around the best deals more than ever, if they buy at all,” said Counterpoint Senior Analyst Maurice Klaehne. “This year’s holiday sales cycle will look quite different from usual.”

#2963. Etihad’s New Credit Cards Are Primarily for Status Chasers

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site or when you click to or take an action on their website. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

The new cards offer perks like faster paths to status and elevated earning rates when purchasing tickets with partners.

Etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two new credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for new applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in New York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

The earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

Plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

Those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.)

One of the most interesting perks of the new cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

#2962. Tired of Sudden Outages? Your Go-To Prep Guide for Everyday Disruptions

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Online > Online Services

Don't let AI failures or cyberattacks disrupt the services you rely on.

These beefy portable power stations can keep your fridge running during emergencies.

If you haven’t already been affected by one of the multiple major system outages that have taken place in November, count yourself lucky. Starting with a Nov. 12 Microsoft outage that kept people’s Outlook email from reaching them for hours and culminating most recently in a Nov. 22 Delta system outage that left travelers stranded, it’s been a rough month. Those incidents are part of a larger wave of disruptions across the US, including a nationwide ground stop of all air travel, an outage affecting classified national security communications and a disruption of online banking services.

Even worse? The month’s not even over yet.

With legacy systems struggling to handle updates and AI tools occasionally going haywire, it’s smart to brace for more outages ahead — and potentially bigger ones.

Governments globally are advising households to stock a basic supply checklist for potential emergencies — guidance that has inadvertently fueled public anxiety and online conspiracy theories.

If you haven’t already stocked up on supplies or made a plan for how you’ll handle a power blackout, a lengthy internet outage or a utility problem that could affect your water or sewage service, you shouldn’t wait.

“Emergency preparedness is NOT just about earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, severe storms or wildfires,” said Chris Reynolds, an emergency management professor and expert from American Military University. “As we all rely on digital infrastructure to conduct the business of our daily lives, a disruption in electricity through accidental or nefarious actions can interfere with banking, communications, online shopping and access to our favorite websites.”

Reynolds’ advice is simple: Prepare, but don’t panic.

“Family emergency preparedness is not a one-time thing,” Reynolds said. “It’s practice that should be continuous.”

Short-term internet, cell and website outages may be the easiest to deal with because they happen so often. We’ve been trained to either wait it out, reset our home router or try an alternate device.

If you have internet connectivity but can’t access certain services, visit Downdetector to see if others are experiencing the same issue. The site shows the number of people who’ve filed a report about an outage and places the most recent and severe outages at the top of its homepage.

Cell service outages are sometimes confined to one of the major service providers; it can be helpful to have a backup mobile device, like a phone or tablet, or an internet hotspot that uses a different cell service so you have a backup if necessary.

If internet service is out for a long time, however, it could cause major problems.

“We are all used to having all of our records stored on our computers or in the cloud,” Reynolds said. “It is important to have an offline version or paper copy of important records, emergency phone numbers, etc., in the event of electrical or digital infrastructure failures.”

While many people go cashless these days, a sustained internet outage could disrupt payment systems. It’s wise to have at least a modest amount of cash on hand. (No need to spring for gold bars just yet — dollars are fine.)

“The whole idea is to have a plan that works when technologies fail,” Reynolds said.

Luckily, November’s outages didn’t include a widespread electricity blackout, but experts have not ruled out the possibility of one in the future. It could even happen nationwide.

No matter how widespread the blackout is, the advice on how to prepare is largely the same as you might follow during winter storm outages or blackouts caused by summer power grid strain. Make sure you have portable chargers available and ready to charge devices like cell phones. Keep supplies, like water, flashlights and batteries, food and a first aid kit, in your home, as suggested by Ready.gov.

For sensitive data devices, like backup drives and computers, a UPS (uninterruptible power supply) is a must.

Portable power stations that can power even large appliances, such as refrigerators, have become popular among those worried about utility uncertainty. Devices that can quickly jump-start a car and emergency hand-crank radios, which can keep you in the know during a lengthy blackout, are other good supplies to have.

A lack of power could affect your family’s medical needs, especially for those who use home ventilators or refrigerated medications like insulin.

“Families should discuss a specific backup plan with their healthcare providers,” Reynolds said. “It is not advisable to power medical equipment with portable generators.”

Carbon monoxide poisoning can be a danger for those using gas-powered portable generators trying to power medical equipment during a blackout. Do not use them indoors or in enclosed spaces.

Utilities have become increasingly popular targets for hackers.

If you lose water or gas service, contact your utility to see how widespread the problem is and how soon it will be fixed.

For water disruptions, it may be necessary to boil water before drinking it, if you’re able to. Shutting off the main water valve to your home could prevent burst pipes later. Don’t flush your toilets when there’s a water or wastewater disruption.

While a gas outage simply means your supply has been interrupted, a rotten-egg odor or a hissing sound signals a dangerous gas leak. If you’re unsure and can’t reach someone at your utility, call for help from a safe distance.

Keep some shelf-stable pantry staples on hand in the event of service disruptions or widespread outages that may continue for an extended period.

“Remember, the goal is to have enough to sustain a family for a finite period of time,” Reynolds said. “It is not hoarding or stockpiling.”

“Finally, and most importantly, decide in advance how family members will reconnect if separated during a crisis or emergency,” Reynolds said. A predetermined meeting spot avoids confusion when you can’t reach each other.

For more information on emergency supply kits and what to include on your list, check out Ready.gov.
